card.text: The first quasar identified, in the early 1960s, and the brightest in our sky.

sources.label: ESA/Hubble potw1346a: ESA/Hubble & NASA
sources.locator: caption: the first quasar ever to be identified, in the early 1960s; of these very bright objects, 3C 273 is the brightest in our skies; quasars are powered by a huge disc of particles surrounding a supermassive black hole

introduction.text: Hubble's view: the glare of the core hides the galaxy around it, and the faint streak to one side is a jet of matter it throws out. The picture is flat and has no depth.

optical.title: 3C 273 and its jet
optical.summary: The cross is the telescope's diffraction of a point of light; the faint streak is the jet. A flat picture, with no depth.
